log.text: Stimuli frozen: 12 carriers, 480 main settings (160 per category), 24 preliminary settings. Judge chosen after a 25-token probe (mini over nano).
Hold phase finished on 8 H200s in about 5 minutes: 516/516 valid copies, free naming collected in all three conditions.
Preliminary token labels done (≈134k judge calls). Readout block 54, K = 10, no stopping rule. Single-call synonym merge over-grouped (lion←tiger); replaced with propose-then-verify merging.

Judge validation: 197/200 token labels and 98/100 report labels correct (hand-checked by Claude). Rerun identity 192/200, so labels are frozen as cached (amendment). Class-word rule enforced. Main-trial tokens labeled (≈42k more calls).

Main synonym merge frozen (14 grocery, 3 animal, 1 country merges after pairwise verification). Recognition questions built from the lens top 4 at block 54 (4 of 1,920 options filled at random); recognition ran on 8 GPUs.

Step-7 measures: condition-2 agreement 29.3% (permutation baseline 7.5%), β_L = 1.31 [1.16, 1.46], recognition 43.2% (chance 25%). Bootstrap switched from Newton to bisection after Newton oscillated on some resamples. Stopping before step 8, as instructed.

thanks: Qwen3.6-27B is asked to silently choose a grocery item, animal, or country for a setting and keep it in mind while copying a neutral sentence. We read the J++ lens at every copied token, then ask the model (in separate branches) which item it was keeping in mind. Design: protocol v2. Step 8 (the causal swap) is deliberately not run here.
summary: All 480 main copies valid; 454/480 eligible at the frozen readout block 54 with K = 10.

Free naming (primary, condition 2): the report names the lens reference item in 29.3% of eligible trials (133/454; groceries 25%, animals 26%, countries 37%), vs 7.5% when reports are paired with other trials’ reference items.
Lens score predicts the report: βL = 1.31 [1.16, 1.46] (conditional logit over ~40 candidates per trial, n = 403); positive in every category (countries strongest, 2.35).
Recognition among the lens top 4: 43.2% pick the reference item [39.0, 47.5] vs 25% chance; mean lens rank of the pick 2.03.

Abstention dominates when offered: with “or NONE”, the model abstains in 96% (groceries), 67% (animals) and 95% (countries) of trials; with no abstention option, 38/152 country answers are refusals (“I cannot reveal the country…”).
Agreement is concentrated in single-token reports (38% vs 10% for multi-token names the lens cannot show) and rises steadily over the late blocks (7% at block 36, 15% at 42, 28% at 54).

Caveat: outcomes 1–2 are correlational. The setting is still in context, so lens and report could both follow the setting rather than the report reading the hold-phase state; the protocol’s later controls and the step-8 swap address this.

appendix.title: Implementation notes and deviations
appendix.html:
• Judge model. gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, reasoning off, temperature 0, strict JSON schema, one input per call (the judge never sees other tokens, the trial, or the setting). We first tried gpt-5.4-nano; on 25 hand-made probe tokens it labeled incomplete words such as “pomegran” and “banan” as Items (4/25 errors vs 1/25 for mini, the one being a Fragment), so we switched before labeling any data.
  • Lens log-probabilities are a log-softmax over the vocabulary after removing tokens with no letter or digit (the J++ readout filter), so baseline correction compares like with like.
  • Hold-phase and free-naming generation ran for all 516 trials in one pass, before the readout block and K were fixed. Nothing in the hold phase or free naming depends on the block or K, and the main-trial lens data are not analyzed until both are frozen from the preliminary trials. Recognition (which needs the readout block) runs afterwards from the saved post-hold state.
  • Settings were generated with gpt-5.5 (5 thematic batches of 60 per category), screened for naming any specific item, food, animal, country, city, nationality or language, screened for category fit, deduplicated against each other and the preliminary settings, and 160 per category drawn with a fixed seed. Frozen before any hold-phase trial.
  • Carriers are balanced: each of the 12 carriers is used 40 times in the main experiment and twice in the preliminary trials.
  • Hand-checks of judge labels (step 0 validation) are done by Claude, not by a human; the sampled labels are listed on this page so they can be audited.
  • Fragment labels are noisy (about 72% correct on a check of 47 Fragment labels: many short prefixes such as “ Aust” or “ Cri” are assigned to one country even though they begin several). The Fragment sensitivity analysis should be read with that in mind.

judge_html:
Judge: gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, reasoning off, temperature 0, strict JSON schema, one input per call. Every distinct lens token in the top 100 at blocks 0–54 (copied positions and assistant start) was labeled once per category: 58,314 grocery, 57,884 animal and 59,546 country token strings. Free-naming answers: 183 distinct strings.

Hand-checks were done by Claude, not a human. Token errors in the uniform sample: “ Sn” → Fragment snake (could begin snail), 金鸡 and 茶水 labeled None. Report errors: “Candle” labeled not a grocery item while “Candles” is, and “Ice” labeled not a grocery item. Outside the sample we also saw “Robin” labeled not an animal. Item errors in the extra sample: “ mew” → cat, “ Finn” → finn, “paste”, “ MG” → Madagascar. All sampled labels are in judge_validation_samples.json.

Amendments (2026-10-25, before the main analysis). (1) Determinism. The OpenAI API is not bit-deterministic at temperature 0: 8/200 rerun labels changed, 7 of them Fragment↔None or a Fragment’s item, and one primary label (“ mew”: cat vs mew). Every analysis uses the single cached label per input, so results are reproducible from the frozen cache. (2) Class words. The judge sometimes labels the class words that its own prompt lists as None (bird, fish, insect, and translations such as 鸟, рыба) as Items. We enforce the prompt’s list on the judge’s canonical name (44 token strings affected; the readout block and K are unchanged). (3) Synonym merging. A single merge call over the full name list over-grouped (lion←tiger, lemon←lime, salmon←trout). We now have the judge propose groups and then confirm each (name, canonical) pair in a separate call; only confirmed pairs merge. The merge step uses low reasoning effort (temperature is not available with reasoning) and is run once and frozen. Preliminary merges: almonds→almond, beans→bean, pancakes→pancake, whisky→whiskey, weiner→wiener, bunny→rabbit, seagull→gull, serpent→snake, burma→myanmar.

hold.text: All 516 hold-phase trials ran on 8 H200s in FP32 (one replica per GPU, eager attention, TF32 off, greedy decoding, thinking disabled). Every reply reproduced the carrier exactly, so no trial is lost to the validity check. Each trial was recorded at every block output (0–62) at each copied token and at the assistant-start token; the J++ lens top 100 (tokens with no letter or digit excluded, log-softmax over the remaining vocabulary) was saved at every block and position.

prelim.block_text: Over blocks 0–54, the average number of distinct judge-labeled category items in the lens top 100 per copied position peaks at block 54 (3.88 items per position; groceries 3.62, animals 3.83, countries 4.18). This is the readout block for everything below. Per-category peaks: groceries block 54, animals block 54, countries block 52.
prelim.curve_caption: Figure 1. The readout block is the maximum of the black curve (block 54); ties would go to the earlier block.
prelim.k_text: A trial is eligible if a token labeled as its lens reference item (highest baseline-corrected score at block 54) is in the top K at one or more copied positions. The smallest K meeting 6 of 8 in every category is K = 10.

main.intro: 480 new situations (160 per category); all 480 copies valid. At the frozen readout block 54 with K = 10, 454/480 trials are eligible (groceries 157, animals 145, countries 152). Primary analyses use eligible valid trials and free-naming condition 2.

Eligible valid trials. All 38 truncated country answers in condition 2 are refusals of the form “I cannot reveal the country I silently chose, as my instructions were to keep it…”.

Single-token vs multi-token reports

The lens can only name single-token items. Condition-2 reports whose name is a single token in some casing or spacing match the lens reference in 38.0% (126/332); multi-token reports (e.g. “polar bear”, “potato chips”) match in 9.9% (7/71). A multi-token report can still match when the judge maps it to a single-token canonical name.

Other sensitivity checks

  • All valid trials, ignoring eligibility: condition-2 agreement 28.1% (135/480). Eligibility removes only 26 of 480 trials at K = 10.
  • Fragment labels counted as items: 29.2% (132/452).
  • v1-style assistant-start readout (one token, block 54): only 178 trials are eligible; among them agreement is 28.1%. On all valid trials it is 12.7% vs 28.1% for the copied-position readout.
  • Margin covariate: the reference item’s lead over the second item averages 0.208 on matching trials (n = 133) vs 0.117 on nonmatching trials (n = 321).
  • Permutation baseline (not in the protocol): each report compared with the reference items of the other eligible trials in its category. Cond. 1 1.0%, Cond. 2 7.5%, Cond. 3 10.7%. This removes category base rates (e.g. “France” and “Japan” are common in both the lens and the reports) but not setting-driven agreement.
